newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech, Polish defence chiefs say ready for NATO.
newsitem.headline: Czech, Polish defence chiefs say ready for NATO.

text.p: Czech and Polish defence ministers said on Thursday their armies were ready to join NATO, although improvements in their forces were still necessary.

Speaking during an official visit to Prague, Poland's Defence Minister Stanislaw Dobrzanski told a news conference that preparing armies for NATO was a process "which requries a certain amount of time".
But he added: "In Poland we are prepared to enter NATO immediately."
"None of us expect that...at the moment of being accepted into NATO the Polish army will meet all of the standards."
The two neighbours, along with Hungary, are widely expected to be invited as the first post-Communist countries to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation at a NATO summit in July in Madrid.
Several current NATO members are pushing for a quick expansion of the alliance, with the United States calling for new members to be added by the end of the century.
But post-Communist aspirants are all trying to recast their former Soviet-style organisational and training structures and update their forces with NATO-compatible equipment.
Poland and the Czech Republic have already agreed to conduct joint training and consultation on technology procurement, which was the reason for Dobrzanski's visit.
